candidates.attacker_control: The SVG author controls URI-valued attributes such as xlink:href of <image>, <use>, <feImage>, <cursor>, <font-face-uri>, <color-profile>, <script> and any CSS url()/@import value. No authentication or special privileges are needed: the attacker only has to get the SVG parsed/rendered by a Batik-based service (for example batik-rasterizer, PNGTranscoder/JPEGTranscoder, or any application that reuses SVGAbstractTranscoder with default hints).
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Verified that the bridges do perform a check (SVGImageElementBridge.java:199-206, URIResolver.java:128-136), so the flaw is not a completely missing check; the defect is the permissive default strategy. Verified that DefaultExternalResourceSecurity (same-host policy) exists but is not returned by UserAgentAdapter, and that it additionally compares only host names and unconditionally allows data: and local file: references when docURL has no host (DefaultExternalResourceSecurity.java:77-98). Verified that batik-svgbrowser/JSVGViewerFrame and batik-swing wrap the check differently, but the library transcoder path (relevant for server-side rendering) uses the inherited permissive default. Considered that Batik documentation describes the UserAgent as the place for integrators to install their own policy; however, the shipped default used by the transcoder/rasterizer still permits arbitrary origins/protocols, which is the behavior later tightened in Batik's SSRF fixes. Not runtime-confirmed.
candidates.impact: Server-Side Request Forgery: when a Batik-based server renders or converts untrusted SVG, the attacker can make it issue HTTP(S) requests to internal/loopback services, follow redirects, and read local files via file:/jar: URIs. Depending on the target this enables internal service enumeration/abuse (metadata endpoints, admin APIs) and disclosure of local image/SVG/text content that Batik can decode or embed; it also forms the delivery primitive for the chain of Batik SSRF CVEs fixed after 1.9.
candidates.prerequisites: The application transcodes/renders attacker-supplied SVG with the default Batik user agent (the standard transcoder/rasterizer configuration; KEY_EXECUTE_ONLOAD defaults to false, but external resources are still resolved during GVT build, so scripting is not required). The attacker's reference must resolve to a URL Batik can open (http/https/file/jar/data), and for file: reads the target must be readable by the Batik process and parseable as an image/SVG for content disclosure.
candidates.root_cause: UserAgentAdapter.getExternalResourceSecurity() returns a RelaxedExternalResourceSecurity instance whose checkLoadExternalResource() body is empty, i.e. every URI scheme and host is allowed. SVGAbstractTranscoder's user agent (SVGAbstractTranscoderUserAgent extends UserAgentAdapter) does not override this method, so the default used by ImageTranscoder/rasterizer accepts all external resources. Every bridge that resolves URI-valued SVG attributes then calls this no-op check before opening the stream (SVGImageElementBridge.createImageGraphicsNode -> openStream; URIResolver.getNode for use/tref/mpath/patterns/filters; SVGColorProfileElementBridge; FontFace; CSSEngine.parseStyleSheet), so an xlink:href/href value supplied by the SVG author is dereferenced without any effective origin/protocol restriction. The stricter DefaultExternalResourceSecurity that exists alongside it is not the library default and compares only host names (not scheme/port) anyway.
candidates.title: Untrusted SVG can force Batik's default transcoder to load arbitrary external resources (SSRF / local file access) because the default UserAgent returns RelaxedExternalResourceSecurity
candidates.trace: 1) Application calls an SVGAbstractTranscoder (e.g., PNGTranscoder) on untrusted SVG; SVGAbstractTranscoder.createUserAgent() returns SVGAbstractTranscoderUserAgent (SVGAbstractTranscoder.java:136-138), which extends UserAgentAdapter without overriding getExternalResourceSecurity. 2) Document contains e.g. <image xlink:href="http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/" ...> or xlink:href="file:///etc/passwd". 3) SVGImageElementBridge.buildImageGraphicsNode parses the href into a ParsedURL and calls createImageGraphicsNode (SVGImageElementBridge.java:155-181). 4) createImageGraphicsNode calls userAgent.checkLoadExternalResource(purl, pDocURL) (SVGImageElementBridge.java:199-206). 5) UserAgentAdapter.checkLoadExternalResource delegates to getExternalResourceSecurity(...), which returns new RelaxedExternalResourceSecurity(...) (UserAgentAdapter.java:362-393). 6) RelaxedExternalResourceSecurity.checkLoadExternalResource() has an empty body, so nothing is thrown (RelaxedExternalResourceSecurity.java:33-37). 7) The bridge then opens the attacker-chosen URL (SVGImageElementBridge.openStream -> purl.openStream(...), SVGImageElementBridge.java:410-416, called at line 245) and the response is read/decoded; the request has already reached the internal endpoint/local file. The same no-op check path is used for <use>/<tref>/<mpath>/gradient/filter references through URIResolver.getNode (URIResolver.java:128-136), for color profiles (SVGColorProfileElementBridge.java:123-124), web fonts (FontFace.java:149, 206) and external CSS (CSSEngine.java:1165-1168).
candidates.unverified: The exact upstream fix commit/CVE identifier for this snapshot could not be verified from source alone (no VCS metadata, no changelog in the snapshot). The SSRF candidate is consistent with Batik 1.9.0-SNAPSHOT and the post-1.9 SSRF fixes, but the benchmark's labelled issue could instead be one of the rejected leads below; no exploit was executed and no external service was contacted.
candidates.weakness_type: Server-Side Request Forgery (CWE-918) / improper external-resource origin restriction (CWE-441)

coverage_summary: Assigned source scope: 1804 readable files under the repository root (all batik-* modules plus test-sources/test-resources), no binary or sensitive-name exclusions reported. Inspected broadly: XML parsing/entity handling (SAXDocumentFactory, SAXSVGDocumentFactory, XMLResourceDescriptor, DOMUtilities, XMLPreferenceManager), external-resource and script security (UserAgent/UserAgentAdapter, Default/Relaxed/Embeded/NoLoad security strategies, BridgeContext, URIResolver, DocumentLoader, all element bridges that resolve xlink:href, CSSEngine, FontFace, CursorManager, ScriptingEnvironment/BaseScriptingEnvironment), scripting interpreters (RhinoInterpreter, RhinoClassShutter, BatikSecurityController, DocumentJarClassLoader), transcoder/rasterizer defaults (SVGAbstractTranscoder, SVGConverter, Main), svgbrowser GUI parsing (XMLInputHandler, NodePickerPanel, JAuthenticator, preference/main defaults), serialization (AbstractDocument/SVGOMDocument readObject), URL handling (ParsedURL/parsedURL protocols) and codec entry points. Did not exhaustively audit numeric parsing/rendering code (batik-parser, batik-gvt, batik-svggen, batik-codec internals) or every test resource.
limitations: No VCS metadata, CHANGES file, or CVE references are present, so the snapshot date and the benchmark's labelled vulnerability/CVE could not be confirmed; the reported candidate is the strongest source-evidenced issue, not a verified CVE match.

Some upstream resources are absent from the snapshot (e.g., META-INF/services handler registrations and *.policy files referenced by build.xml/Main.java), which limits certainty about default reachability of the svgbrowser XML handler and about the actual SecurityManager policy used by the rasterizer.

No code was executed, no dependencies/versions were resolved, and no runtime confirmation was performed; JDK/parser/Xalan behavior (e.g., default redirect following or XSLT extension functions) is described from source-level expectations only.
Coverage of very large rendering/parsing modules was targeted rather than exhaustive, so other memory-safety/DoS-style defects in parsers and image codecs may exist but were not traced.

rejected_leads.lead: XXE / untrusted-XSLT in batik-svgbrowser XMLInputHandler.handle (DocumentBuilderFactory.newInstance() + TransformerFactory.newInstance() with no disallow-doctype-decl / secure-processing / external-access restrictions; parses the user-opened .xml/.xsl at batik-svgbrowser/src/main/java/org/apache/batik/apps/svgbrowser/XMLInputHandler.java:166-172 and transforms with the attacker-supplied stylesheet at lines 186-211). Also NodePickerPanel.parseXml (lines 846-869) uses a default DocumentBuilderFactory on user-supplied XML.
rejected_leads.reason: Real textbook XXE/unsafe-XSLT code, but it is desktop/GUI-reachable (requires a user to open a malicious .xml/.xsl in Squiggle), and the service registration file (META-INF/services/...SquiggleInputHandler) is not present in this snapshot to prove default reachability. Kept as the strongest alternate lead, not submitted because the candidate above is reachable by default in the server-side transcoder without user interaction.

rejected_leads.lead: Remote code execution through the Java-archive script type: SVGConstants.SVG_SCRIPT_TYPE_JAVA (application/java-archive) is included in SVGAbstractTranscoder.DEFAULT_ALLOWED_SCRIPT_TYPES (batik-transcoder/.../SVGAbstractTranscoder.java:840-845), and BaseScriptingEnvironment.loadScript (batik-bridge/.../BaseScriptingEnvironment.java:391-438) downloads the referenced JAR, reads META-INF/MANIFEST.MF and instantiates the Script-Handler / SVG-Handler-Class classes, giving arbitrary code execution when scripts are executed.
rejected_leads.reason: Requires script execution to be enabled (rasterizer -onload / KEY_EXECUTE_ONLOAD=true, or Squiggle where load-Java defaults to true) and a same-origin check passes for attacker-hosted documents; the transcoder default is executeOnload=false, so this is a configuration-dependent RCE rather than a default-path finding. Not confirmed to be the labelled issue.

rejected_leads.lead: Unsafe deserialization/reflection in AbstractDocument.readObject (batik-dom/.../AbstractDocument.java:2720-2738): the serialized class name is passed to Class.forName and then to getDOMImplementation/newInstance.
rejected_leads.reason: Requires the hosting application to deserialize attacker-controlled Java streams containing Batik documents; no in-project path deserializes untrusted data, so reachability/security impact could not be established from source.

rejected_leads.lead: Script-driven SSRF in ScriptingEnvironment$Window.getURL/postURL (batik-bridge/.../ScriptingEnvironment.java:1073-1140 and the URLConnection POST path around lines 1170-1180) opening or posting to arbitrary URLs without checkLoadExternalResource.
rejected_leads.reason: Only reachable when SVG scripting is enabled; scripting is disabled by default in the transcoder and the URL(s) are supplied by the script rather than the document markup. Same root-cause family as the submitted candidate, so not split out.

rejected_leads.lead: CursorManager.cursorHrefToFilter falls back to ImageTagRegistry.getRegistry().readURL(purl) (batik-bridge/.../CursorManager.java:514-516) without repeating the external-resource check.
rejected_leads.reason: The URIResolver call earlier in the same method (line 458) already performs the check and a failed security check is rethrown, so with a restricting user agent the fallback is normally not reached; with the permissive default it is the same submitted root cause.

summary: Reviewed the Apache Batik 1.9.0-SNAPSHOT source snapshot (1804 visible files: all batik-* modules, test-sources/test-resources). The strongest source-evidenced issue is that Batik's default user agent used by the SVG transcoder/rasterizer permits loading every external resource regardless of origin or protocol, so an untrusted SVG processed server-side can make Batik fetch arbitrary URLs or local files through ordinary SVG features (xlink:href on image/use/feImage, CSS, fonts, color profiles). The individual bridges do call UserAgent.checkLoadExternalResource, but the strategy returned by the default user agent is a no-op, so the check never denies anything. This matches the Batik SSRF vulnerability class fixed after 1.9. Other plausible leads (svgbrowser XXE, application/java-archive scripting, document deserialization) are noted as unconfirmed/rejected rather than additional candidates.
